classes.name: Oral corticosteroids
classes.description: Systemic oral corticosteroids: prednisone (tablets, solution; Rayos delayed-release appears discontinued), methylprednisolone (Medrol, dose pack), prednisolone (solution, Orapred ODT, Millipred), dexamethasone (tablets, solution, Dexamethasone Intensol, TaperDex/Dxevo/HiDex packs; Hemady 20 mg is labeled for multiple myeloma only, an alternative, never the pick), hydrocortisone (Cortef; Alkindi Sprinkle and Khindivi oral solution for children). Deflazacort (Emflaza) and vamorolone (Agamree) for Duchenne are specialty alternatives only, never the pick. Not budesonide (Entocort, Uceris, Tarpeyo) or inhaled/topical steroids.
classes.plainDescription: Short courses of steroid pills that calm inflammation fast, for flares of asthma, COPD, arthritis, allergies and more.
classes.indication: Inflammatory flares, asthma/COPD exacerbations, autoimmune disease, adrenal insufficiency

preferredAgent.plainSig: Take with food in the morning, at the dose and for the days your prescriber sets.

records.verificationNote: Steroid rows on PDF p.38-39 (printed p.22-23). Pick prednisone 10 mg tablet, Tier 3, no PA. Prednisone tablets are listed in 1 to 50 mg strengths; the 10 mg tablet is the strength chosen for the sig. Emflaza (deflazacort) is the only listed specialty steroid: PA and limited distribution, so it is a paRequired item. Hemady, Rayos, Alkindi, Khindivi, Agamree, Orapred ODT, Millipred and the dexamethasone packs have no row; recorded nonformulary under the closed-formulary statement. Vamorolone and Khindivi appear in the description only and are not listed. [Sonnet check 2026-11-13: Brand-only nonformulary rules rest on the guide's own wording: "Brand name medications not listed in the medication list are not covered" (PDF p.2) and "Brand Name medications are covered only if they are included in the Closed Formulary list" (PDF p.3); exception route: Coverage Exception Process, PDF p.12 (printed XI). The p.5 line "any medications not on the formulary ... are not covered" is overridden for generics by "All generic medications are covered unless specifically excluded by your plan" (PDF p.3), so no generic is recorded as nonformulary from absence.]

records.verificationNote: Read from the formulary text layer, row by row (each tier digit sits on the same row as its drug name; pypdf gave no x-coordinates for the digits). Formulary sig and quantity limits are as printed; the document prints no sig, so the sig is the label starting dose. Prednisone 10 mg tablet is Tier 1 with no PA; BvsD is a Part B versus Part D review flag, not a PA, so it is not in preferredRestriction (PDG p. 61). Not listed: Rayos, Medrol, Orapred ODT, Millipred, Cortef, TaperDex, Dxevo, HiDex. Hydrocortisone tablets print on p. 54 (in the list's dermatology block) and are cited as printed. [Sonnet check 2026-11-06: tiers and flags re-read in layout (row-aligned) extraction, not flattened text; nonformulary reasons reworded to the front-matter wording; prednisone tablets carry BvsD (Part B vs D review, not PA); dose pack does not; added Rayos and Khindivi as not listed.] [Reused: same national Humana Premier Rx PDP formulary]
